covariates.label: COMED zone load forecast
covariates.description: Day-ahead forecast of load in the Commonwealth Edison (COMED) zone in MW — the zone whose price is the target.

rationales.rationale: COMED shows its largest negative seasonal departures concentrated in the middle‑late window (notably steps in the mid teens relative to its cycle); given COMED is the local driver, that concentrated below‑normal load supports a stronger downward effect on price in steps 14–18.

System load is lower versus one week earlier across much of the horizon (horizon mean mildly below recent), a broad but modest decrease in system demand that can exert a moderate downward pressure on price from roughly step 9 onward.

COMED (local) load forecast is modestly below its recent typical level (horizon mean ≈ -0.3 sd) and shows consistently negative seasonal departures; as the zone's direct demand driver this supports a mild downward effect across the full window.

Day‑ahead system load is below its typical seasonal level (horizon mean ≈ -0.4 sd) and especially depressed relative to the same phase one week earlier (consistent -0.8 to -1.7 sd), with the largest negative departures concentrated in the middle hours; this supports a clear downward pressure on price, strongest in the mid-window.

COMED (local) load forecast is materially below its typical level for the horizon (horizon mean ≈ -0.7 sd) with negative same‑phase departures throughout and the strongest negatives concentrated in the mid‑day/peak hours. Because local load directly drives zonal price, apply a stronger downward adjustment during the peak window (steps 9–18 = '--') and milder downward adjustments in the early and late segments (steps 1–8 and 19–24 = '-').

PJM system load is modestly below its typical level for the horizon (horizon mean ≈ -0.3 sd; same‑phase departures generally negative), so expect a mild, broad downward pressure on zonal price relative to the target-only base. The signal is consistent but not large, so apply '-' across steps 1–24.

COMED load forecast is substantially below recent levels (horizon mean ~ -0.6 sd; ~ -1.1 sd vs the last-24), with consistently negative seasonal departures across hours — COMED load strongly supports a broad downward pressure on COMED price.

System load is modestly below recent levels (horizon mean ~ -0.1 sd; ~ -0.5 sd vs the last-24) with small but consistent negative seasonal departures — supports a weaker, across-the-window downward effect.

COMED exhibits mixed early/late departures (small negatives in the very early steps and positives later), so the overall COMED signal across the whole window is ambiguous for an across‑the‑board adjustment; leave COMED at 0 for the full window in this read.
System load is consistently modestly elevated relative to recent baseline (+0.6 sd vs the last 24 and ~+0.65 sd end‑to‑end), which supports a mild, broad upward pressure on price across steps 1–24.

COMED is the local demand driver for the target. The forecast shows small above‑normal same‑phase departures in the early hours (steps 1–10), which should nudge price mildly above the target‑only base (+). From the late morning through the peak (strong negative same‑phase departures centered in the mid‑teens, especially steps 14–19) the local load is well below typical for those hours and the horizon mean is below normal, supporting a strong downward push on price (--) in that peak window; the neighboring hours (12–13 and 20–24) show more moderate below‑normal departures and so get a milder downward judgment (-).

PJM system load is modestly below its typical seasonal level (horizon mean ≈ -0.3 sd) and the seasonal departures turn negative in the mid‑to‑late horizon; this broad but modest reduction in system demand supports a mild downward adjustment on price from about step 16 onward (-). Early small positive same‑phase departures do not provide a clear upward push, so earlier steps remain 0.

adjusted.rationale: Judge fixes a mild positive effect in steps 1–10. The base is low in this span (mean ≈ 21.01) and the local COMED signal in-window is mixed but the fixed sign calls for an upward nudge. A small positive per-step shift of +2.0 raises the early-hour base modestly without overcorrecting.

Judge fixes a mild downward effect for steps 12–13. The base is elevated here (mean ≈ 36.14) so a modest negative translation is appropriate. A per-step reduction of -3.0 implements a conservative downward correction consistent with the fixed mild negative judgment.

Judge fixes a strong downward effect for the peak entry (steps 14–15). The base is substantially high in this window (mean ≈ 43.65), so a pronounced negative per-step correction is warranted. -6.0 per step captures a strong downward translation while remaining a measured adjustment against the current base.

Both covariates are fixed strongly negative across steps 16–19 and the base is very high in this core peak span (mean ≈ 57.14). A larger per-step reduction of -8.0 reflects the combined strong negative judgments and the high current base, producing a substantial downward correction in the mid‑afternoon peak.

Both covariates are fixed mildly negative in the late window (steps 20–24) while the base is only modestly above average (mean ≈ 33.63). A moderate per-step cut of -4.0 implements the combined mild downward influence without overreacting.

adjusted.rationale: Judgment calls for a mild upward tweak in steps 1–10. The base for these hours is low (steps 1–10 mean ≈ 21.01) and the target lookback sd is 12.64, so apply a small positive per‑step correction (+1.0) to nudge the base slightly upward while respecting the judged mild strength.

Judgment is a mild downward adjustment for steps 12–13. The base there is elevated (steps 12–13 mean ≈ 36.14) but the judgment strength is modest, so apply a small negative per‑step correction (‑1.5) to reflect the mild downward influence.

Judgment is a strong downward adjustment for steps 14–15. The base is relatively high for these hours (steps 14–15 mean ≈ 43.65) and the judge indicated a substantial negative effect, so apply a sizeable per‑step reduction (‑6.5) to reflect that strong downward pressure.

Combined judgments call for a marked downward adjustment for steps 16–19 (strong local negative plus a mild system negative). The base is high in this window (steps 16–19 mean ≈ 57.14) and the combined strength warrants a large per‑step negative correction (‑7.5) to reflect the net strong downward influence.

Judgments for steps 20–24 are moderate downward (both local and system mild negatives). The base is near typical for these hours (steps 20–24 mean ≈ 33.63), so apply a moderate per‑step decrease (‑3.0) consistent with the judged mild-to-moderate negative effect.

rationales.rationale: COMED day-ahead load is materially weaker in the mid-late horizon versus the recent-week benchmark and is modestly below its seasonal norm in these hours; lower local demand should exert a strong downward influence on the COMED price in that span.

PJM system load forecast is modestly below typical for the second half of the window (horizon mean slightly negative vs recent norms); that broader demand softness supports a moderate downward pressure on price across the later hours.

adjusted.rationale: Judge calls for a mild downward correction. The current system_load signals are only modest (steps 11-13 ~+0.5 sd vs recent; 20-24 ~+0.1 sd) and the base forecast for these hours is only slightly above recent norms (means ~34.7 / 33.6 vs 24h avg 31.11). Given the weak supporting anomalies, apply a small negative tweak of -0.5 $/MWh per step to reflect the mild downward pressure without overcorrecting.

COMED is judged to exert a strong downward influence and system_load a moderate downward influence for these mid-late hours. The base forecast in this span is notably elevated (mean 52.64 vs the 24-step avg 31.11) so a substantive downward adjustment is warranted. Balancing the strong local effect against mixed load signals, apply a moderate-strong downward correction of -3.0 $/MWh per step (~0.24 target SD).

rationales.rationale: COMED load forecast runs below its recent-week and seasonal benchmarks across much of the late window (horizon mean below its recent norm); this supports a moderate downward adjustment to price through those hours.
System-level load is close to its recent-cycle level on average (horizon near neutral and only modest departure from the last 24 steps); not enough consistent signal to move the base forecast here.

adjusted.rationale: The fixed judgment is for a moderate downward correction. Current-window evidence shows a pronounced end-to-end fall in COMED load (-2.34 sd) and a modest shortfall versus the same phase last cycle (-0.5 sd), while the base forecast in these hours is somewhat elevated (steps mean 42.79 vs recent 24-step mean 31.11). Taken together this supports a noticeable but not large downward per-step adjustment; I apply -3.0 price units to each hour 12–24.

rationales.rationale: COMED load shows only modest deviations from its recent-24-step level outside the pronounced mid-window dip, so no systematic adjustment across the full window is warranted in this reading.
Compared with the same phase of recent cycles and the week-earlier values, system load shows a modest dip in the mid-window hours; a localized moderate negative effect on price is plausible there.

adjusted.rationale: The fixed judgment calls for a localized moderate negative correction in the mid-window. With the target lookback sd = 12.64, a per-step downward adjustment of about 0.4 sd (≈ -5.0) achieves a moderate, localized reduction without overriding the relatively high base forecast for steps 15–19 (base mean 55.05).

rationales.rationale: There is a concentrated shortfall in the COMED load forecast relative to its recent-week pattern in the late-mid hours (a sharper negative departure in that narrow span); a short, moderate downward influence on price is therefore reasonable for those hours.
System load is only mildly below some seasonal benchmarks but near-neutral on average for the window; no adjustment from system-level load is applied in this minimal attribution.

adjusted.rationale: Judge indicates a short, moderate downward influence on price for these late-mid hours. The COMED covariate shows a strong end-to-end downward run (−2.37 sd) though with some mixed short-term offsets; the base forecast for these steps is somewhat elevated (+0.3 sd). Balancing the fixed negative judgment against the mixed short-term signals yields a moderate per-step downward correction of −5.0 (≈0.40 of the target SD = 12.64).
